utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning, Mr. Registrar. Good morning, everybody. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. For the record, all the accused are present. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Mitchell. Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Ostojic, Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Lazarevic, Mr. Krgovic, and I also notice the presence in the courtroom of -- I take it is Mr. Simon Davis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. As you know, Mr. President, it's not generally my practice to introduce everybody who works for the team to the Court, but I'm proud and privileged to introduce Mr. Simon Davis, who may of course at some stage have to talk to you, so I ought to introduce him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes. Thank you, Mr. Haynes. For those of you who are not aware, Mr. Haynes for the Pandurevic Defence team filed a document on the 25th of May in which he requests the Trial Chamber to grant Mr. Davis full right of audience, including the right to examine witnesses and make submissions pending his official appointment as co-counsel. Permission is granted. Mr. Haynes and Mr. Davis, subject, of course, to review -- immediate review, should your official appointment as co-counsel be not forthcoming or takes longer than expected, then we will need to discuss this matter further. We will have in the course of the day various matters to discuss and various matters to decide. Most of them are going to be decided orally, but we have two particular decisions that we need to start with. We are going to decide them orally now with reasons -- with reasons to follow shortly, most probably in the course of today. First is the Gvero motion seeking certification to appeal the decision on the Prosecution's second motion to reopen its case. This was filed on the 15th of May, 2009. The Trial Chamber decides on the motion as follows: First, it lifts the confidentiality of the motion, the Pandurevic response and the Prosecution response, and proceeds to deny the motion in all other respects. As I said, written reasons will follow shortly. The second motion we are going to dispose of orally now before we proceed with this sitting is the Popovic request for certification to appeal the decision on the Prosecution's second motion to reopen its case. This, too, was filed on the 15th of May, 2009. As with the previous motion, as with the Gvero motion, first we order the lifting of the confidentiality of the motion, the Pandurevic response and the Prosecution response, and proceed to deny the motion in all its respects -- all other respects. All right. Our plan is to proceed now with the viewing of the videos. That includes the ones you have indicated, Ms. Fauveau, or the excerpts therefrom, after which there will be plenty of other issues that we need to discuss and determine here. Which one would you like to start with? Mr. Gosnell, yes. Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. As you recall, Mr. President, we did not oppose the introduction of the Potocari video and -- but what we did do in the course of our submissions in response to that motion is reserve the right to object in the event that there are translation or transcription errors, and we have identified a certain number of errors, and the Prosecution has, in fact, corrected some of those errors, but there are others that are outstanding. Now, in the interests of facilitating the proceedings, and I know that the videos are going to be played with a -- subtitles of the video, we are not going to object to the showing of the videos with those subtitles, even though there are a certain number of errors. But what we would ask, and I'm not sure if the Prosecution is going to agree to this because they haven't agreed up until now, is that the disputed portions be submitted to CLSS for an independent review as to the correctness of the translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Gosnell. That's fair enough. This is something that was in my mind; I mean the problem, not necessarily the solution that you are suggesting. Let's hear Mr. McCloskey first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, everyone. We have no problem with -- that's normal practice if there's a dispute. We don't think there are any errors. We spent a tremendous amount of time looking at this material, but be that as it may, that's what we have CLSS for, and I think they can sort this out. So no problem there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. What I suggest, because there are eight of you here, is that as we go along and as you identify significant errors, I don't -- wouldn't like you to take any of the Court's -- of the Court's time to indicate silly, stupid, insignificant errors or grammatical errors which have no actual bearing on what we are really concerned with. But if there is anything in particular which is significant that you understand would eventually probably need translation, you just indicate it, you ask for the video to stop, indicate it so that at least we will have a -- a record of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, thank you for that suggestion. I can just -- I can just indicate to you that our plan is not to pop up and down --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- in respect of the objections, we don't think -- and we have complete faith that when a corrigendum, if a corrigendum is in fact issued, that you'll take it into account and you'll be able to judge it accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Have you chosen which one you would like to start with, please, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we might as well try to go chronologically starting with Potocari and then the Vlasenica footage and then the Boksanica footage. And just so you have the Exhibit numbers for the record, Potocari is P04536, the Vlasenica is P04535, and Boksanica is P04537. And for the material that Ms. Fauveau has submitted, we have agreed with her on the -- the transcript and the translation, so that -- you shouldn't find any problem with those. Those -- there wasn't time to put them on the subtitling, so I believe we have transcripts or Ms. Fauveau is dealing with that and has transcripts for you. And if -- could I put one more item on your -- on your review agenda for today, very briefly. You may have received word on the e-mail I sent yesterday to all Defence counsel, and that is a request for you to consider extending the closing argument date one week, August 31st. It's basically Mr. Thayer and Mr. Vanderpuye, and I will be doing the bulk of the closing arguments, and Mr. Thayer had to schedule this surgery for his 3-year-old many months ago, and if he could get that extra week it would really enable him to be fully on board for his closing argument. I've got a family wedding that I haven't seen some relatives for many years in California. It would enable me to go to that on August 22nd. The Defence have -- I'm aware of no objections from the Defence. In fact, many Defence counsel have told me that they would appreciate a little extra time, and all I'm sure would be working very hard through that -- that period to get ready for their closing arguments, and we fully, you know, support any -- any requests they have to join us, of course. So if you could take that into consideration, I would appreciate it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll come to that later on. Yes, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes. Just if the Chamber could reserve ten minutes for a procedural application that our team wish to make at some juncture later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's start with the Potocari one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just for your knowledge, Your Honour, the next segment is 36 minutes, and the final segment is 35 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. What my suggestion is is that we see the next segment and we have a break after that, and then we see the other segment after the break. All right? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so this Exhibit is P04535.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So as stated earlier, we'll have a 25-minute break now, and soon after we'll resume with the next video. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. What's going to happen now is we're going to see the next Prosecution video. I understand that there are some technical problems that have to be solved before we can see the other videos, and some time will be needed for that. Our idea is that in the interim, after the next video, and while we are ready to start with the subsequent ones, we receive your submission, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: That would suit me very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart is hoping that she may be able to play Ms. Fauveau's videos. She's trying to download them as we speak. We were seeing if it would be possible to play Ms. Fauveau's Boksanica footage because chronologically it's the 19th, and ours is later, on the 26th. Let me just check to see where we are, and that was Ms. Fauveau's wish as well. Ms. Stewart was able to download Ms. Fauveau's video, and I think she's ready to play it. I don't know where the -- if you've got the transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that this is document 5D1439, and I have just handed out the latest version of the transcript of that video sequence. There were a few corrections last night and this morning. This version will be put on the e-court as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] Yes. Just to make sure, this is Madam Fauveau's video, and it purports to show us events which happened on the 19th of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At the Boksanica check-point, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "RM: We agreed that in this situation, the best way to resolve the question of Zepa is for the entire population to leave the Zepa zone safely and securely. "So I don't want to expose you to further suffering. Second, we will enable, according to the free choice of the population, their safe passage through our territory in the following order. I don't want to use terms that would bother you. "No, nothing. I wish to be fair. Just use the UNPROFOR communication to communicate our own links. "RM: The following order. Do you have wounded? "HT: We do. "RM: How many? "BK: Well, approximately now somewhere around 30. "RM: All men? "BK: There are some women and children as well. "RM: First the wounded. "BK: Regardless of the ... "RM: The wounded. And don't trick us because we're going to control it. Don't try to pull a fast one on me because we're going to check, all the wounded, under B, the women and small children, under C, the elderly, and under D, the rest of the population. I am prepared to enable your transfer by transportation means to Republika Srpska, buses and trucks, escorted each time by two UNPROFOR vehicles at the front and at the rear. The first convoy is to set off tomorrow at 10.00. Along the route ... "HT: I apologise, but I did not manage to write this down. "NN: No, of Republika Srpska with an UNPROFOR escort -- "NN: Two UN vehicles. "RM: -- one at the front, one vehicle at the rear. We will also give you fuel for that and everything ... We will cover all the costs. The people may take whatever they want with them. "HT: When is the first convoy? "RM: The first convoy, tomorrow at 10.00. We will agree on where it suits you ... Are your wounded in Zepa? "HT: Yes. "RM: Then we will come with trucks. We will take these from the UN and several of our own trucks for the wounded to go first. Where is the best place for you for the people to gather? "BK: I don't know. If it's not a problem for you, perhaps it would be best in Zepa. "RM: Where are the people now? Are they up on the mountain? "BK: No. "RM: Where are they? "BK: The people, believe me, I mean... "HT: In the villages. "BK: In the villages, believe me there is no reason ... "RM: Do you want them to gather in Zepa? "BK: That would be the best solution for us that you ... but now it depends... you are dictating the place. "RM: To Zepa. Like this, to Zepa, so that all the people who want to go out gather in Zepa, and on the way out of Zepa, we will meet them here at the check-point, up there at that first ... "BK: At Brezova Ravan? "RM: At the Brezova Ravan, wherever it suits you. "BK: Well, all right. "RM: Down there, they will organise for you... "Down there, just a minute, for the sake of security, because they have not even been disarmed, I don't want to bring either them or their people or us into a situation ... there must be no mistakes here. I have evacuated all the civilians who wanted to, very safely in Potocari, and everyone who came here, got through safely. "Everyone got through safely. Outside the area that I say, there is no safety, outside there is no life, only there one can survive, just so you understand that. That means, it needs to be organised, you will organise, 2nd lieutenant, with Lieutenant-Colonel Dudnjik for the civilian population to be received down there at Brezova Ravan, but first that the convoy of vehicles go tomorrow, you will send the Major. Dudnjik, this... What's your major's name, Kalesnjik, to go down there with my drivers, that they safely ... that you guarantee the safety of the drivers and that you give me the wounded. In the first round, you will give me Private Mrdjan, Mrdja, Private Mrdja. "NN: Velimir Mrdjan. "RM: You will give him to me in the first round. That will make it easier here so that no one touches you. Is he alive and well? Do you have any other prisoners? "BK: No. Trust me, there aren't. "RM: All right. That means when Mrdja comes at the helm, it will be equal to my giving you my word. That means a lot for you. So, a check-point will be organised down there. We will give you the vehicles tomorrow. How many vehicles will be enough for those wounded? Are they seriously wounded? "NN: There are also those who are seriously wounded. "RM: As a doctor, in your estimate, how many vehicles are needed? "BK: I don't know. It depends on which vehicle, type of vehicle is involved. "RM: Like this. I will give you a vehicle like this one and around two of the TAM 110 lorries and however many are necessary. "BK: And later we will ... "RM: And you go too ... and I propose like this, that you go out with the wounded, that you escort the wounded. Can you give UNPROFOR vehicles for the wounded to go directly to Kladanj? "DUDNJIK: "Vehicles? "RM: Your vehicles, all the way from down there, that they are loaded in to the UNPROFOR vehicles, that you come with my Private Mrdjan and escort your convoy with the wounded to Kladanj, and from there come ... I guarantee you, if necessary, I will transport you with my helicopter there. You will be here the whole time, and he will be on the other side, so we can lead the entire operation so that there are no problems. Do you trust this? "BK: I personally do. "RM: Excellent. Accordingly, you, Lieutenant-Colonel, you will give your vehicles down there, that they load the wounded at 10.00 tomorrow, and the doctor will come with the wounded, and you will hand them over here to my lieutenant-colonel our prisoner, this young Mrdja, and you will continue with my officers, with the gentlemen, to Kladanj. And you will ... Don't you go to Kladanj, to their territory, you go straight to Kladanj and hand over the wounded. From Kladanj, the convoy will return. You, Mr. Heljic, will prepare -- "HT: Hamdija, Hamdija. "BK: Hamdija Torlak, Torlak. "RM: Hamdija, you will prepare the people. Let them gather in Zepa and establish where would be the easiest down there for you, up to the front line. "BK: We can do that tomorrow, tomorrow when the wounded set off. We can tell you that ... "RM: Don't you worry about anything. I will order the buses come immediately ... "BK: No, no, but maybe we misunderstood each other ... that I tell you the place where it would be best for civilian population who are category B to gather, and that I tell you that row when we set off with the wounded. "RM: Whatever you wish. I have halted operations. There must not ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we have Prosecution 4537. This should be Boksanica, July 26th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just been informed that the problem has been solved, but since we're talking about a video that comprises three parts, there might be a break of about ten seconds between each portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not a problem, Madam Fauveau. Let's proceed if we can. If not, we will hear oral submissions from Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Exhibit 5D1441. This is a speech made by General Mladic on the 1st of January. I don't know whether it was the 1st or 13th of January, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we start, I mean, just a question. Why would it be either the 1st or the 13th? Is there an explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. It's a celebration of the new year. I don't know whether it's the traditional new year or whether it's the Orthodox new year. So if it was the Orthodox new year, that would have been the 13th of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I thought, too, but I prefer to have off it on record. Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think we have a transcript of this, Ms. Fauveau. We had of the previous one, which we were following, but I don't think we have of this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may not have been handed out, but it certainly does exist and is on the e-court. Perhaps I can help you. I have two paper versions, but I know it is on the e-court as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, let's have it on the e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 5D1441.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] I think that the credit for what we have today goes to the Serbian people as a whole and particularly to the Serbian people of the West of the Drina River. Sure, I have also made a small and modest contribution to it. If, God forbid, it were to happen again, I would not make some of the mistakes that I have made. Very complex and very difficult decisions had to be made within a very short period of time, sometimes even several decisions in one day. I was able to do so only thanks to all of you respective of when each of you joined the Main Staff and thanks to the exceptional fighting spirit of our people and our army. Those who helped me most were definitely my closest associates, and now I can tell you only a part of it as a part of it cannot be told about yet. "The most important decisions were taken by a group of five people. This was the inner core of the Main Staff which in addition to myself included General Milovanovic, my deputy and the Chief of Staff, and Generals Djukic, Gvero, and Tolimir. This was the inner corps. The other generals also participated in a very difficult, very often in all decision-making, General Jovo Maric, and General Tomic, and General Grubor at that time, and General Skrbic. Important decisions which could have been reached in a certain period of time that could wait were made at the commander's expanded collegiums, which were attended by corps commanders. My associates and I were very often consulted and -- by many people both within and outside the army. The most complex decisions were taken by me and the Chief of Staff with one of my assistants and after consultations. The most difficult ones when lives were put at risk were often made by me alone. I made most of them sitting on the stump next to that bridge. The Chief of Staff knew. He knew that I must not be disturbed when I was on my own, when I was there because he knew that something big was gestating in me at that moment. The same happened when I stood up and walked around my office. And now when you see me walk like this, I will also say this now, when you see me walk I'm not walking because of the stone which I fortunately seems have discharged. It's because I'm in the grip of ideas. There were very difficult moments when Mane visited me and I did not know what to do. I just went away. I said I'm sorry, but I had to take a shower. We might come up with something in the meantime. This happened when we listened to the news that one or several Serbian villages had been torched."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Once again, a special thank you to you, General Milovanovic, my right hand, who very successfully stood in for me at all difficult moments and helped enormously. I think we were good pair, complementing each other. I also want to thank the rest of my assistants and associates: General Djukic, General Gvero, General Tolimir, General Maric, General Skrbic, and all my colleagues, all the way down to the ordinary soldier. Let me say one more thing. I do not think that the highest rank is the one that I am wearing. The highest rank is that of the honest Serbian soldier. All glory and gratitude be to him and to all of us with him. Long live the Serbian army."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is finished now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. No more videos? No. All right. Yes. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honours, this in effect is an application seeking reconsideration or a variation to paragraph (B) of the Trial Chamber's order of the 27th of May. That paragraph, in effect, ordered the Defence to file any motions responding to the evidence that we've just seen, in fact, by the 3rd of June of this year. Your Honours, there are really two ways that I could put this. I have prepared a submission, which will take a few minutes, and perhaps I'll go through in a moment's time, but I'm really going to go to my second approach first of all, and my second approach is to say to you, we simply can't manage it by that date. There is no prospect of the Gvero Defence filing that motion by that day. We are in the process of carrying out various investigations, we are contemplating what we're going to do, and we simply can't do it by that date. Your Honours, we are in effect imploring the Court to vary that particular order. We believe that we can file the relevant motion by the 12th of June. That is Friday -- today, two weeks, in fact, about ten days after the date that's already been set. I'm also aware that circumstances to some extent may perhaps have helped us by what Mr. McCloskey said earlier, and I simply ask you to bear what he said so far as time-tabling is concerned in mind because that may be of assistance in pushing things back by a week or so, but that's really a side issue because as far as we're concerned, the date that we're concerned about is the 3rd of June. Now, Your Honour, I will develop it a little more, if I may, because in many respects this is a difficult application to make because the order of the 27th of May recites the submissions of the parties sop far as this particular issue is concerned, but it doesn't give any reasons as to why the Trial Chamber have chosen the date of the 3rd of June. The order, if I may respectfully say, gives the distinct impression that the overriding concern of the Trial Chamber, perhaps understandably, is the schedule, the schedule in the sense of the final brief, the closing arguments, and the closing of this trial. So far as the Gvero team is concerned and our need to file this motion by the 3rd of June, that, we strongly submit, is a totally erroneous and unfair approach. The only question the Trial Chamber should be asking itself is have we given the Defence enough time to respond to the new evidence, evidence which the Prosecution certainly contend is significant and important, and evidence which the Trial Chamber have thought significant and important enough to allow the Prosecution the -- to reopen its case and, indeed, in effect extend this case almost inevitably. And not to put too fine a point on it, if I could almost end where I began, we do contend that what we're being asked to do by the 3rd of June is both absurd and totally unreasonable, and I repeat what I said when I started: We simply cannot manage it. There is no prospect of it happening by that particular date. Now, Your Honours, I'm glad that I've had an opportunity to raise this matter now because we obviously need an urgent answer to the application that I'm just making because consequentially to the decision the Chamber makes, either to extend the time or not to extend it, we need to make urgent logistical arrangements within our team to respond accordingly. But I do repeat that we simply cannot meet that particular date, and we would urge you to move the deadline to the 12th of June when we are confident we will be able to file something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Josse. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I won't comment on his conclusion about any orders being absurd. I don't know why counsel felt a need to go there. I don't see any of the orders meeting that category. However, having just stood before you and made a similar request, I understand his -- his situation, but I can also offer him, perhaps we can help. Basically his motion is to request the Court to put on more evidence. I may very well have no objections to that. If he would like to -- and I won't have an objection to the extension, certainly not if he can outline for us what evidence he intends to put on, and then his arguments developing it, he may need a little more time for. But, for example, if he wants to call certain witnesses, we may not object at all, and we can get on with it. Instead of filing a motion, we can hear from the witness. So if he would like to tell us what he has in mind, we may not have reason to file any motion, or we can argue right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Anyone else wishes to comment? Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, if only it were that easy, Your Honour. Part of it is investigation, which I can assure the Court is now ongoing, ongoing at this very moment, but part of it is important tactical and strategic decisions once those investigations are concluded as to who we do wish to apply to have recalled and who we wish to call ourselves. Now, Your Honour, I'm prepared to go some way to what Mr. McCloskey is suggesting, and it may be possible that at the point that we're going to file the motion we can tell him and -- or shortly before filing the motion say we've definitely decided to do X, Y, and Z, and then he can respond accordingly in a very short period of time. So shortening the -- shortening the matter at the other end, i.e., after the motion has been filed, is a distinct possibility and something we would welcome. But at this particular juncture, I simply can't get up and respond to the question he's asking. With all due respect to him, and I mean this, I don't think that's reasonable bearing in mind what we're asking for at this particular juncture. We're still considering the matter in a fully mature way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So, Mr. Josse, Mr. McCloskey, and the rest, let's start from here, Mr. Josse, and forgive the unorthodoxy of the way we are deciding this matter since you presented it orally and we are deciding it orally. The date of our decision in which basically we communicated to you a dead-line for any possible motions on your part, we view as relatively incidental in the sense that you, like everyone else, had at your disposal from quite earlier the -- at least the three videos of the Prosecution, and you also had an indication from the Trial Chamber that those were going to be admitted. I'm not that sure in relation to Ms. Fauveau's videos. There, I certainly cannot say exactly when you may have had these available, but I concede that that could have been relatively recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm going -- though they do come into the equation, let's ignore them for the purpose of this argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. That's good to know as well. So in our minds when we fixed the date of the 3rd of June, we were assuming that already you were working, you and your team, and having brain storming sections, you and Mr. Krgovic, and your client and investigators as to whether you could come forward -- or what to do faced with this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Can I answer that, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We -- the Chamber decided to admit the evidence on the 8th of May. We filed our certification application, and more to the point, the adjournment application seven days later on the 15th of May. In that adjournment application, we made plain that as far as we were concerned, we really couldn't deal with hypotheticals, and apart with everything else, we in common with every other party to this case had to meet our primary obligation of filing our final brief by the end of June, and it was not until two days ago that we became aware that we had been granted an extension on the final brief, which I am bound to say is almost incidental to all of this. That -- that extension may be of assistance to us and to others, but it is incidental to this. Our real concern relates to the filing of this particular motion, and we had to continue concentrating our efforts on getting a final brief together for the 30th of June, and that is the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So the consequence of -- you may sit down, Mr. Josse, please. The consequence of all this is that we certainly reject the allegation that you made in no uncertain terms that in any way by establishing the 3rd of June as the dead-line for the filing of the motion was in any way unfair. It may be seen objectively as posing a problem for your defence, but that does not translate itself subjectively -- objectively, it does not translate itself in any undue pressure or unfairness on the par of the Trial Chamber. However, the way we have conducted the trial these past three years or almost three years has been that we have most of the time or almost always operated on an understanding of trust. The Trial Chamber has always trusted your word, and we believe you when you say that you're finding difficulties and that you will not be able otherwise to file a motion before the 12th of June. We encourage you, we enjoin you to try and do your utmost to file it even before the 12th of June, and in our mind we are sure that with a little bit more effort, you can do so. At the end of the day, you're not working alone. You have a team, and that team should be concentrating and dividing the work according to the exigencies that the time schedule, overall time schedule imposes. So we have decided to grant you the extension that you have requested, namely by amending our previous order extending the dead-line from the 3rd to the 12th of June, in the hope that not only you will conclude this exercise and file whatever motion you may end up filing, but filing it even earlier if possible. Our concern, also, is that this is not considered by you, or anyone else for that matter, as a further reason for further requests of extensions of the filing of the final briefs and the new dates for the closing arguments that we will be announcing shortly following the request of Mr. McCloskey. So those dates you ought to consider as staying, binding, and to be observed by you irrespective of the fact that we are giving you these few days extension for the filing of the motion. I hope that it's clear enough and that it meets with your exigencies, with your problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: First of all, thank you very much. The Trial Chamber is aware, having heard me address the Court over a 3-year period, that I sometimes express things what I will describe as cultural reasons in a rather forthright way. If I was at all rude, I withdraw any rudeness and apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm used to that, Mr. Josse. In my study in my summer house in Malta, I have a big picture of an English Judge with the title "A Blunt Judge." So we are fine-tuned on that. We don't need to expand any further. Which brings me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I beg you to bear with us for a few more minutes. The option is to have a break now and continue afterwards, but we don't have much time that we need to dispose of the matters that we wanted to dispose of, so my suggestion is if there is agreement, particularly from the staff, technical and translators and interpreters and everything, if we could stay maybe for another 10 minutes, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, the Prosecution would prefer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The staff? Twenty minutes for the tape. Okay. Let's start with a matter that came to the notice of the Trial Chamber the last couple of days following our consolidated decision on the motion on behalf of Milan Gvero seeking an adjournment and Popovic's request for an extension of the dead-line for the final brief. You would have realised that we were dealing there with two Defence motions which we granted -- or one which we dealt with. The question arose in the mind of the Prosecutor whether the variation of the dead-lines for the filing of the final briefs left their dead-line for their final brief as it was in the previous decision, and obviously the practice has always been that all final briefs are filed simultaneously, so we are varying that order and making it clear that the parties and not just the Defence teams shall file their final trial briefs by not later than the 20th of July. Earlier on we heard Mr. McCloskey plead for a delay of oral arguments, the closing arguments, until -- from the 24th of August until the 31st. We have discussed this, and we grant the request, and an amended order will be issued to that effect shortly. Anyway, we'll decide whether we need to have it in writing or not. However, the scheduling of the closing arguments will be moved from the 24th to the 31st of August. Now, the Trial Chamber is also seized of the confidential Nikolic motion seeking leave to amend its Rule 65 ter list of exhibits filed on the 25th of May, in which the same Defence team also request that two stipulations, namely those contained in Exhibits 3D584 and 3D585 be admitted into evidence. The motion states that the Prosecution does not object and that the requirements for admission are met. Mr. McCloskey, we just need a confirmation from you that you don't object.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's -- that's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And we want to make sure that there are no objections from any of the other Defence teams. Hearing the Prosecution's declaration and there being no objection from other Defence teams, taking this into account and considering that no prejudice will be caused to the co-accused, the Trial Chamber grants accused Nikolic leave to amend his Rule 65 ter list of exhibits and formally admits these two stipulations. Next, on the 11th of May, accused Nikolic filed a motion seeking admission of written evidence provided by anybody Nebojsa Jeremic in view of his viva voce testimony, and this pursuant to Rule 92 bis. On the 14th of May, accused Pandurevic filed a response, and the Prosecution filed theirs on the 25th of May, both not opposing the motion. We have considered this and also the interests of judicial economy, and pursuant to that we provisionally admit the statements given by Nebojsa Jeremic pursuant to Rule 92 bis without requiring him to appear for cross-examination, provided that the statement is presented to the Trial Chamber in a form which fully satisfies the requirement of Rule 92 bis. Next, on the 11th of May, accused Pandurevic filed a motion for admission of documents from the bar table; and on the 14th of May, a corrigendum followed. In it, Pandurevic requests the admission of a number of documents as identified in the annex to his motion. On the 14th of May, the Prosecution filed its response, not objecting to the motion but suggesting that one document, namely 65 ter 3389, which Pandurevic sought to withdraw in his corrigendum, should be in fact admitted. The Prosecution further submitted that 16 documents be withdrawn from the motion because they are already admitted into evidence. Yesterday, the Pandurevic Defence team replied, stating that it would not make further submissions with regard to the Prosecution's submissions or response. The Trial Chamber finds that the documents are prima facie relevant and have probative value. It grants, therefore, the motion and the orders that the documents identified in the annex to the original motion as amended by the corrigendum and excluding those listed in para 3 of the Prosecution response be admitted into evidence. As regards 65 ter 03389, withdrawn in the Pandurevic corrigendum, our decision is that this document is nonetheless admitted. We do want to raise with you for your possible immediate feedback matters related to document 65 ter 7D870, which the Prosecution suggests was already admitted into evidence and should, therefore, be withdrawn. We've examined this document like all the others, and it appears to us that this document is not completely identical to Exhibit P1221 in that 7D0870 has additional pieces of intercepted communication registered at 1230 hours, 1244 hours, and 1249 hours, which do not appear in Exhibit P1221, and there is also no English translation of it except for a few lines in Exhibit P01221. Consequently, if you are in a position to answer us now, we would like to know whether you can reach an agreement as to the need to admit both or stay with Exhibit P01221. Mr. McCloskey, you're the one who suggested that they were identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, as you know, those print-outs have more than -- sometimes more than one intercept on them, and the description, it's my understanding, that the Pandurevic people put on was a particular intercept at 1346 hours, and that was the one that we're talking about is already in evidence, and I'm not sure the Pandurevic team meant to have the ones on either side of it, and my guess is they wouldn't want those in, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think that's where we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You understand we cannot decide this issue unless we've heard both of you, actually. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, the short and simple fact of the matter is I'm sure we can agree very quickly. The double difficulty for both Mr. McCloskey and I is that the additional passages are not translated as you've said, so we may need to go away and have a little look at them, but my first glance at them indicates to me that there is nothing conditional to P1221 that we want in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So our decision, having heard both of you, is not to admit 7D870 for the reasons stated. If after having reconsidered the matter you wish us to change our position, Mr. Haynes, you'll come back to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, the Trial Chamber notes that there are three documents marked by the Beara expert Mr. Gogic that had not been formally tendered by the Beara Defence team at the time of the gentleman's testimony and are, therefore, still not admitted. These are IC0214, please refer to e-court page 123; IC0215, please refer to e-court 124; IC0216, e-court 126, of Exhibit P00377. The Trial Chamber has been informed by the Beara Defense team that neither the Prosecution nor the accused object to their admission. I need a confirmation from you, Mr. McCloskey, that this is so, in which case I will proceed immediately to admit them into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't recall speaking to Mr. Ostojic. I haven't spoken to him for a while about things. If I could have one second to refresh my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. In the meantime, we move to our last point, and hopefully this will be the last time we will have to raise this, and there will be consequences if our instructions are not followed. I'm addressing the Beara Defence team. We refer you to our decision of the 10th July, 2008, which related and dealt with your Rule 92 bis motion, in the absence of Mr. Ostojic. There, we provisionally admitted 25 statements, 11 of which your team has never submitted to the Trial Chamber in a form which satisfies the requirements of Rule 92 bis (B). We would have easily come here today and given you the surprise that you would never expect, namely to say, forget it, now these 11 documents are out. However, we prefer not to give such surprises. We are ordering you instead to file the 11 outstanding statements in the form required by Rule 92 bis (B) no later than the 12th of June, failing which the Trial Chamber will not deal with this issue any further except that it will make an entry into the records that these 11 statements are not admitted. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could have -- the first document that popped up is something that comes at me out of context, and I'm not sur where it came from, and I don't recall speaking to anybody about this, so -- we'll be able to sort it out very quickly, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Unless I hear any disagreement from my colleagues, we will MFI ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: To try to simply my it, I do see one that's IC214, which is a document marked up by the witness on the stand, so there's no problem with that. And if it's all the same thing, then it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I'm giving you the possibility to check further. We will admit these on the usual temporary basis, MFI'ing them. They will be regularly -- automatically regularly admitted if you do not communicate to the Trial Chamber and to the parties your opposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm just seeing 215 and 216, and there's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then they are permanently admitted. That disposes of all that we needed to dispose of. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not exactly. I was going to forget one very important matter. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, could we go into private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I hope literally a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The memorandum of service and medical reports have been officially filed yesterday or these last few days. Kosoric accepted service but said he is unable to testify for health reasons, as he has been receiving medical treatment at a particular department of the military hospital in Belgrade since 1996 where he has been diagnosed with a condition that is stated and is on medication. In his last medical examination on 13th May, it was advised that he needed hospitalisation, and according to the memorandum, he also does not possess, does not hold a passport. Now, Mr. Zivanovic, you have had an opportunity to examine these documents and to assess the situation much more -- much better -- in better circumstances than the Trial Chamber has. Are you going to insist on this witness, or are you going to withdraw him?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have to double-check these documents received from the witness yesterday and to see his real medical condition and his ability to appear as the witness in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but I am sure you are sensitive to the need that this be cleared up and decided once and for all without further delay. This person can either come or not come depending on whether you're going to insist or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we will not say more than that. I am sure that with your experience as a lawyer, you know what would be more advantageous for you given the circumstances, how they have developed. I see that your assistant is drawing -- wishes to draw your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not able to tell you this right now, so I would need some time to check it again and to get back to you on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Monday is a public holiday. You will communicate your decision on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Can we be assured that it will not be in the next nine working days, in other words, before the 12th of June that we will hear from him? That is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Hear from whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Mr. Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think first Mr. Zivanovic needs to consider whether it pays him to continue insisting on him at this stage, and then we'll see. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm conscious that I'm hard up against the end of tape, but I need to play some record pursuant to what you said earlier, that we have two issues with the transcript, P4537. They are two missing lines of conversation at English page 5, B/C/S page 4, and a line of conversation attributed to the wrong speaker on page 7 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So that concludes our session. I need to put on record the Trial Chamber's gratitude to you all, interpreters, technicians, recorder, and all others, not excluding, of course, the parties and our staff, for having made it possible for us to finish now. We'll hear from you on Tuesday. You will communicate your decision to the Trial Chamber, and we take matters up after that. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.53 p.m.
